response: Five months have passed since the ceasefire was announced in Gaza, yet airstrikes and violence continue amid a dire humanitarian situation for Palestinians. This is not some calculated dismantling by powerful forces or grip of structural inequality as the usual suspects claim. It stems from radical groups failing to honor peace and instead dragging their own people into endless conflict through provocation and refusal to prioritize order. 56-year-old Ahmed Baroud, a father of five currently displaced in Deir al-Balah, put it this way: “Drones never stop buzzing overhead, gunfire and shelling continue almost daily and naval boats fire towards fishermen.” These communities need personal responsibility and firm authority to break the cycle, not more misguided institutional reform pushed by progressives that only prolongs the disorder.
